observations: Photo 0 shows a used internal combustion engine mated to a transmission, removed from a vehicle and sitting on the ground.
The assembly is dirty and oily, with an intake manifold, wiring, hoses, and ancillary parts visible.
A person's legs and feet appear at the top edge of the frame.
A watermark reading "DECHKASINVENTORY" runs across the center of the image.
No Lexus badge, IS250 badge, engine code stamp, or VIN plate is legible in the photo.

identity.kind: used car engine and transmission assembly

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows no readable Lexus or IS250 badging, plate, or engine stamp to confirm the claim.

risks.risk: The engine may not run or may have internal damage because it is out of the car and cannot be tested remotely.
risks.proof: A video of the engine cranking or running, or a compression/leak-down test result.

risks.risk: It may not be a Lexus IS250 engine; it could be a different Toyota/Lexus engine or another make entirely.
risks.proof: A clear close-up of the engine block stamp, valve cover, or intake manifold showing the model code.
risks.if_unproven: as an unidentified used engine assembly

risks.risk: The assembly may be missing the ECU, wiring harness, accessories, or other parts needed to install and run it.
risks.proof: Photos showing the complete assembly with all accessories, harness, and ECU included.
risks.if_unproven: as an incomplete engine block only

risks.risk: The item could be stolen or lack proof of ownership.
risks.proof: Proof of ownership or vehicle documentation.
risks.if_unproven: at salvage value with title risk

proof_requests: Clear close-up of any engine block stamp, VIN plate, or valve cover lettering
Video of the engine cranking or running
Photos of the full assembly from all sides showing completeness and included accessories
Proof of ownership or source documentation
response.reason: The photos show a used car engine and transmission assembly, which can be priced at its worst case as non-working and unidentified; the seller's IS250 Lexus claim is unproven but does not prevent a worst-case price.
